title: Native derived Hom representatives with the actual source normalization
statement: Fix a finite field $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, and a separated finite-type quasi-compact $k_0$-scheme $X$. Let $\mathcal W$ be the native pro-etale Weil coefficient-module category [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], and let $S=\operatorname{standardHomModel}(\operatorname{ihomBifunctor})$ [def-sf-standard-bifunctor-hom-model]. There exist a derived bifunctor $H:D(\mathcal W)^{\mathrm{op}}\times D(\mathcal W)\to D(\mathcal W)$, representative data $\rho:\operatorname{Representatives}(S.\mathrm{complex},H)$ [def-sf-ringed-two-injective-models], and natural slice isomorphisms $e_L:H(-,L)\simeq\operatorname{derivedHom}(-,L)$. For every K-injective $K$, $(e_L)_{QK}$ followed by the actual $\operatorname{bifunctorRHomOfComplexObjIso}$ at $\operatorname{kInjectiveRep}(L)$ equals $H$ of the identity source and $\operatorname{kInjectiveRepIso}(L)$ followed by $\rho.\mathrm{iso}(K,\operatorname{kInjectiveRep}(L))$. Thus the representative maps compute $H$ for every arbitrary source and K-injective target, are natural in both variables, invert the prescribed quasi-isomorphisms, and the slice identification has the exact native normalization. Only the derived representative extension is asserted; no comparison under forgetting is included.

source.place: Tag 0A95, lemma-RHom-well-defined, and Tag 08J7, section-internal-hom; native product-Hom signs in lean/WeilConjectures/Algebra/Homology/BifunctorHomComplex.lean and native source comparison in lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/DerivedCategory/BifunctorHom.lean.

proof.text: Use the bijection on homotopy classes into a K-injective complex to construct the natural source comparison from each complex K to the actual K-injective representative selected by the inverse of KInjectives.Qh. Applying the fixed-target native Hom functor gives comparison(K,I). For K-injective K this is exactly bifunctorRHomOfComplexObjIso, by the unit/counit equations. For arbitrary K and K-injective I it is invertible: represent K by a quasi-isomorphism into J, and use native source quasi-isomorphism invariance.

Make the already defined fixed-target native derived source functors functorial in the target by postcomposition. The source and target maps commute by the product projection identities. A target homotopy h induces a Hom-complex homotopy whose component at source index p is (-1)^p times postcomposition with h. Expand dS+Sd after each product projection: the source differential terms cancel by naturality and the target terms give the original homotopy equation. Thus the target functor descends to the homotopy category.

Precompose this target functor by the inverse equivalence from the derived category to the homotopy category of K-injectives and uncurry to obtain H. For K-injective I, its unit isomorphism identifies the chosen target representative with I. Compose this target isomorphism with comparison(K,I) to obtain rho.iso. Naturality of the source comparison and of the equivalence unit proves both-variable naturality. Under source and target quasi-isomorphisms the corresponding derived arrow is an isomorphism, so rho.naturality expresses the native Hom arrow as conjugation of an isomorphism and proves rho.inverts.

For each L use exactly kInjectiveRep L and kInjectiveRepIso L. Apply the target functor to the image of kInjectiveRepIso L under the inverse equivalence followed by the target unit isomorphism. This gives the natural slice isomorphism e_L. Functoriality identifies its component with H of the prescribed target identification followed by the target comparison. For K-injective K, comparison(K,kInjectiveRep L) is the actual native bifunctorRHomOfComplexObjIso, proving the stated normalization by associativity. The standard model has the same underlying complex and maps as the native model.

lean.statement: theorem nativeStandardHomRepresentatives [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] : ∃ H : (DerivedCategory (ProEtaleWeilSheaf k₀ l X))ᵒᵖ × DerivedCategory (ProEtaleWeilSheaf k₀ l X) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ProEtaleWeilSheaf k₀ l X), ∃ ρ : Representatives (standardHomModel (ihomBifunctor k₀ l X)).complex H, ∃ e : ∀ L : DerivedCategory (ProEtaleWeilSheaf k₀ l X), Prod.sectL (DerivedCategory (ProEtaleWeilSheaf k₀ l X))ᵒᵖ L ⋙ H ≅ derivedHom k₀ l X L, ∀ (L : DerivedCategory (ProEtaleWeilSheaf k₀ l X)) (K : CochainComplex (ProEtaleWeilSheaf k₀ l X) ℤ) [K.IsKInjective], (e L).hom.app (op (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)) ≫ (DerivedCategory.bifunctorRHomOfComplexObjIso (ihomBifunctor k₀ l X) (DerivedCategory.kInjectiveRep L) K).hom = H.map (X := (op (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K), L)) (Y := (op (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K), DerivedCategory.Q.obj (DerivedCategory.kInjectiveRep L))) (𝟙 _, (DerivedCategory.kInjectiveRepIso L).hom) ≫ (ρ.iso K (DerivedCategory.kInjectiveRep L)).hom
